answer: The kernel of our Sybil resistance architecture leverages ephemeral proof of work linked to verifiable delay functions to bind identity to computational cost, effectively creating a vine of linked cryptographically verifiable reputation commitments across the ocean of network participants. By enforcing a logarithmic penalty function on redundant agent signatures, we ensure that the marginal cost of spawning illicit nodes strictly outweighs potential rewards, forcing all agents into a Nash equilibrium that preserves Byzantine fault tolerance despite adversarial noise.
